slot.brief: Give a keto/aldehyde substrate (e.g. with alpha Hs and without) and ask for the product with a specified reagent: Aldol vs Cannizzaro; pick the correct structure.

stem: 4-Methylbenzaldehyde is treated with concentrated aqueous $\text{NaOH}$, followed by acidification. Which pair of organic products is formed?

verdicts.working: 4-Methylbenzaldehyde has no α-hydrogen, so it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction in concentrated NaOH, yielding 4-methylbenzyl alcohol and, after acidification, 4-methylbenzoic acid.

working:
4-Methylbenzaldehyde has no $\alpha$-hydrogen, so it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction.
$2\,\text{ArCHO}+\text{OH}^-\rightarrow\text{ArCH}_2\text{OH}+\text{ArCOO}^-$
Acidification gives 4-methylbenzyl alcohol and 4-methylbenzoic acid.

Independent check: 4-Methylbenzaldehyde has no α-hydrogen, so it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction in concentrated NaOH, yielding 4-methylbenzyl alcohol and, after acidification, 4-methylbenzoic acid.
solution:
4-Methylbenzaldehyde has no $\alpha$-hydrogen, so it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction.
$$2\,\text{ArCHO}+\text{OH}^-\rightarrow\text{ArCH}_2\text{OH}+\text{ArCOO}^-$$
Acidification converts $\text{ArCOO}^-$ to $\text{ArCOOH}$, giving 4-methylbenzyl alcohol and 4-methylbenzoic acid.
